git.subject: v1: first playable build, not yet measured
git.body:
8 stages, deterministic 60 Hz physics, human play (keyboard + touch),
swarm mode with 100 scripted ghost bots, replay mode, headless harness.
Stage layouts are a first design from the jump numbers on paper
(flat jump about 148 px, jump height about 94 px, pad height about 204 px).
No swarm run was made on the 8 stages before this commit; the bot script
was developed only on the separate "Bot Gym" track.

reviews.review: I like the look: the glowing ghost, a new colour for each stage, and hazards I can read at once. First Steps is a gentle start and Crumble Bridge felt fair and tense. But Spike Garden comes second and I stood in front of a spike for 45 seconds with no way forward; 98 of 100 players failed. Spring Loaded stuck me beside a spring in the same way. Laser Gate killed me in two seconds, before I learned the rhythm. Ferry Lines dropped me in a pit while I waited for a platform. Gauntlet is a wall. I would stop playing at stage 2.
reviews.best: Crumble Bridge: clear, tense, and I can finish it.
reviews.worst: Spike Garden at stage 2 leaves almost every player stuck with no way forward.

reviews.review: I see no difficulty curve here. First Steps teaches gaps and spikes cleanly, then Spike Garden stops everyone: ghosts stand in front of a spike cluster for 45 seconds and only 2 of 100 finish. Crumble Bridge is the one tuned stage, with readable tiles and one saw, but it is easier than Saw Mill and Ferry Lines before it. Spring Loaded is inverted: the low-skill player finishes while better players stall beside the first spring. Laser Gate kills at two seconds with four beams and a faint telegraph. Gauntlet tests springs and lasers together that were never taught; 3 of 100 finish.
reviews.best: Crumble Bridge: a readable new mechanic, one saw as a twist, and an 80% pass rate with deaths that look like the player's fault.
reviews.worst: Spike Garden: stage 2 is a wall that no skill level gets past, so most players never see the remaining six stages.

reviews.review: I want tight, fair routes, and half of this build does not give me one. Spike Garden is broken: the mid player stands beside a spike for 45 seconds and 98 of 100 ghosts fail. Spring Loaded is upside down: the weak player finishes while the strong ones stall before the second spring. Gauntlet stops nearly everybody at the laser-plus-spring chokepoint, so the finale has no flow. Laser Gate kills at two seconds, before I can read the cycle. Saw Mill and Ferry Lines are honest skill checks, and Crumble Bridge is the one stage I would grind for time. First Steps is safe but flat.
reviews.best: Crumble Bridge keeps me moving with a real penalty for hesitation and a clear, fast line to the goal.
reviews.worst: Spike Garden and Spring Loaded stall skilled players with no way forward, which is a route defect and not a challenge.

reviews.review: The game looks good: the glowing ghost, the clear red spikes and a new colour for each stage are easy to read on a small screen. But I got stuck too much. In First Steps the mid player stood in front of two spike clusters for 45 seconds, and in Spike Garden nobody got past them at all; I would close the tab there. Ferry Lines and Gauntlet drop almost everyone into pits, and Laser Gate killed the run after 2 seconds. Crumble Bridge and Spring Loaded are the only stages that feel fair and fun. The difficulty jumps up and down with no curve.
reviews.best: Crumble Bridge is quick, readable and fair, with a real risk but a finish most players reach.
reviews.worst: Spike Garden is stage 2 and nearly nobody can finish it; players just stand at the spikes until the timer ends.

reviews.review: I see no difficulty curve, only a sawtooth. First Steps is a fair opener, but my mid-skill run stood in front of a double spike for 45 seconds. Spike Garden is broken: 0% mid-skill pass and even the expert gave up, at stage 2. Saw Mill and Ferry Lines test moving saws and ferries at 27% and 13% before they teach them. Crumble Bridge and Spring Loaded are the only well-tuned stages, with readable hazards and one clear idea each. Laser Gate kills at 2 seconds with no safe first gate. Gauntlet mixes all mechanics, but 10% pass and a stuck expert make it a wall.
reviews.best: Spring Loaded and Crumble Bridge each teach one mechanic clearly and land in the target pass band.
reviews.worst: Spike Garden at stage 2 cannot be finished by any of the three recorded players, which blocks the whole game.

reviews.review: I like the 10-second routes in Saw Mill and Crumble Bridge: moving saws and crumbling tiles reward a committed line, and Laser Gate has readable telegraphs with real timing risk. But the curve is broken. Spike Garden is stage 2 and stops 90 of 100 ghosts; the mid player stands in front of a double spike row for 45 seconds, and the same freeze appears in First Steps. Ferry Lines drops 87% of mid players into pits, too harsh for stage 4. Gauntlet kills almost everyone at one spring near 35% and even the expert gives up. Spring Loaded is safe but slow.
reviews.best: Saw Mill and Crumble Bridge give a fast, readable sub-10-second line with real risk.
reviews.worst: Spike Garden at stage 2 is a wall that even the high-skill player cannot pass.

  5 tiles after the edge.

git.body:
Measurement (v3): stage 4 mid-skill pass 22.0%, 305 pit deaths. Traces show
bots that ride a ferry and then step into the pit. Cause is in the bot
script: a bot plans with a late view of moving hazards (0-9 frames). The
same late time was used for the platform that carries the bot, so its plan
started from a wrong own position.
Change: plans use the real time for moving platforms; the late view stays
for saws and lasers. Test before commit on stage 4: mid 22.0% -> 45.3%.
Physics and stages are the same as v3. The bots differ from v3 in this
one point.

reviews.review: I like how this looks: each stage has its own colour, and the spikes, lasers and springs are easy to read on a small screen. First Steps is a gentle start, and Spring Loaded is the one I would replay, because the bounces feel generous. Saw Mill is where I would put the phone down. It is only stage 3, the small saws float at jump height, and the recorded mid player died right beside the goal. Spike Garden puts a lot of spikes on me very early. Gauntlet mixes everything fairly, but the dotted laser posts are faint against the dark sky.
reviews.best: Spring Loaded: bouncy, clear, and I can finish it without a cheap death.
reviews.worst: Saw Mill is much too hard for stage 3 and kills players right at the goal.

reviews.review: I like that each stage owns one mechanic and Gauntlet remixes all of them; that is a correct structure. The curve is the problem. Saw Mill at stage 3 passes only 37% of mid-skill players and kills them at 84%, next to the goal, which is harder than the finale. Spring Loaded at stage 6 is then the easiest stage, and its saws sit high off-screen where a spring throws me blind. Ferry Lines gives all three skill levels the same 12 seconds, so the ferries set the pace, not me. Laser Gate teaches well with its dotted telegraph. First Steps kills 29 of 100 with spikes, which is much for a tutorial.
reviews.best: Laser Gate: readable telegraphed beams, deaths spread evenly, and a pass rate that fits its late position.
reviews.worst: Saw Mill is a difficulty spike at stage 3, with moving saws that kill next to the goal.

reviews.review: I like the hazard variety and the readable screens, but the curve is uneven. Saw Mill is a difficulty spike at stage 3: only 37% of mid players pass and my mid run died to a ground saw right at the goal. Ferry Lines is the opposite problem for me: all three skill levels finish in about 12.4 s, so the platforms set the pace and skill saves no time. Spring Loaded has good air routes but little risk. Crumble Bridge, Laser Gate and Gauntlet flow well, though the high-skill death to a Gauntlet laser and the 25 s Spike Garden run look like timing traps, not execution tests.
reviews.best: Crumble Bridge and Gauntlet reward continuous movement and mix hazards without stopping the run.
reviews.worst: Ferry Lines locks every player to the same 12.4 s cycle, and Saw Mill spikes the difficulty too early.

reviews.review: I like the hazard variety and the clean, readable screens. Crumble Bridge and Laser Gate look like real routing stages: commit, keep moving, time the beam. But skill barely buys time. reviews.best: Crumble Bridge and Laser Gate reward commitment and timing with deaths that look like my own fault.

reviews.worst: Saw Mill is too hard for stage 3, and First Steps already kills almost a third of players.

reviews.review: I like that each stage owns one mechanic and Gauntlet recombines all of them; that is correct teaching order. The curve is flat, not rising: First Steps kills 29 of 100 on its first spike row, which is too harsh for a tutorial, and Saw Mill (57%) is harder than Laser Gate (73%). Saw Mill deaths cluster around flying saws whose paths I cannot read from the screen. Ferry Lines and Crumble Bridge have fair pit deaths but little secondary threat. Laser Gate telegraphs its off-beams with dotted lines, which is good. Gauntlet killing the high-skill player on a laser looks like timing luck.
reviews.best: Laser Gate: dotted idle beams make every death readable and the spike-then-laser pairing escalates cleanly.
reviews.worst: Saw Mill: the hardest stage in the set sits at slot 3, with saw paths that are not telegraphed.

reviews.review: I like the readable hazards and the ten-second stage length; Gauntlet chains saws, crumble tiles, ferries, a spring and lasers into a real route, and Spring Loaded and Laser Gate have a rhythm I would grind. But the curve is flat: First Steps kills 29 of 100 at a plain spike strip, and the mid player stood beside it for six seconds, while Saw Mill is the hardest stage at 57% in slot three. Ferry Lines and Saw Mill give all three skills the same time, so there is nothing to optimise. Spike Garden is one repeated jump, and the high-skill run there took 25 seconds.
reviews.best: Gauntlet mixes every mechanic into one fast, readable route with real risk for all skill levels.
reviews.worst: The difficulty curve is flat and out of order, with a tutorial that kills 29% and identical finish times on Saw Mill and Ferry Lines.
